# QS-CFW-3043-62 Quality specification - flange blank CFW-3043-62 (4140)
Revision: Rev E  
This revision supersedes Rev D.  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-3043-62

Scope
- This document specifies quality requirements for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) manufactured from 4140 for Plant P1. It applies to incoming inspection, in-process checks, and final acceptance of forgings designated as flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62).

Requirements
- Material: 4140 as specified on associated manufacturing order.
- Hardness: The hardness range for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is 37-43 HRC.
- Bore tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is ±0.03 mm.
- Weight: The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is 28.1 kg.
- Surface condition: Free of visible cracks, laps, and laps that compromise geometry; surface discontinuities that can be removed by standard finishing operations are acceptable.

Inspection method
- Visual: Inspect for surface discontinuities and check for cracks or laps using good illumination and a calibrated magnifier when required.
- Hardness: Confirm hardness using a calibrated Rockwell C hardness tester capable of verifying the specified hardness range. Record individual sample results with part traceability.
- Dimensional: Measure bore diameter using calibrated bore gauges or compatible metrology equipment. Report measured values against the specified bore diameter tolerance of ±0.03 mm.
- Weight: Verify forging weight on a calibrated scale; ensure no part exceeds the maximum forging weight of 28.1 kg.
- Sampling: Follow plant P1 sampling practices; retain inspection records with part identifiers.

Nonconformance handling
- Parts outside the hardness range, outside the bore diameter tolerance, or exceeding the maximum forging weight are nonconforming.
- Nonconforming parts must be segregated, tagged, and dispositioned per plant P1 procedures.
- Root cause analysis and corrective action are required for recurring nonconformances. Records of disposition and corrective actions must be retained with the inspection record for the affected lot.
